# Overview

This document summarizes the functions defined in [HoTTRijke/chapter3.lean](../HoTTRijke/chapter3.lean).
Each entry includes the function name, its Lean signature, and a short description.

The file is organized into three namespaces: `chapter3_naturals` (a **1-based** encoding of the
natural numbers), `chapter3_integers` (integers built on top of those naturals), and
`chapter3_booleans` (booleans plus small constructive-logic combinators).

The file's header comment notes that starting the naturals from one, rather than zero, "seemed
better" at first for a natural correspondence between naturals and positive/negative integers,
"but this approach has some serious drawbacks and was probably abandoned" — consistent with the
0-based encoding developed in parallel in `chapter3_naturals_with_zero.lean` (see
[its documentation](chapter3_naturals_with_zero_documentation.qmd)), which is the encoding used by
the later `chapter5_props_naturals_with_zero.lean`, `chapter6.lean`, and `chapter7.lean`.

::: {.callout-note}
**A note on implicit/section-variable arguments.** Several definitions below (`myNegType`,
`double_neg`, `double_contrapositive`, `double_contrapositive_ii`, `double_contrapositive_iii`)
do not list their own `(P Q : Type)` arguments. They instead pick up `P`/`Q`/`R` from the
`variable (P Q R : Type)` declaration in scope (`chapter3.lean:255`): Lean automatically
prepends any section variable that is actually used in a definition's stated type as an
**explicit** leading argument (matching how `variable` declared it). The signatures below make
this explicit so they match what Lean actually elaborates, rather than the possibly-misleading
form written at the definition site.
:::

# Namespace `chapter3_naturals`

## Types

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `myN.one` | `myN` | Base constructor, representing 1 in this 1-based natural system. |
| `myN.succ` | `myN → myN` | Successor constructor for naturals. |

## Numeric Constants

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `_1` | `myN` | The number 1. |
| `_2` | `myN` | The number 2. |
| `_3` | `myN` | The number 3. |
| `_4` | `myN` | The number 4. |
| `_5` | `myN` | The number 5. |
| `_6` | `myN` | The number 6. |
| `_7` | `myN` | The number 7. |
| `_8` | `myN` | The number 8. |
| `_9` | `myN` | The number 9. |
| `_10` | `myN` | The number 10. |

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `toStringMyN` | `myN → String` | Converts naturals to strings (`"1"` through `"10"`, and `"≥11"` for anything larger). |
| `myAdd` | `(a b : myN) → myN` | Recursive addition on 1-based naturals; recurses on `b`. |
| `myMult` | `(a b : myN) → myN` | Recursive multiplication via repeated addition; recurses on `b`. |
| `myExp` | `(a b : myN) → myN` | Exponentiation (`a^b`) via repeated multiplication; recurses on `b`. |
| `myMin` | `(a b : myN) → myN` | Minimum of two naturals. |
| `myMax` | `(a b : myN) → myN` | Maximum of two naturals. |
| `triangular_number` | `(a : myN) → myN` | Computes the triangular number of `a`. |
| `factorial` | `(a : myN) → myN` | Computes factorial recursively. |
| `binomial` | `(a b : myN) → myN` | Binomial-coefficient-style recurrence; see *Possible Issues* below for its 1-based limitation. |
| `binomial_v2` | `(a b : myN) → [DecidableEq myN] → myN` | Alternative binomial using `myMin` and a decidable equality check instead of pure pattern matching. |
| `fibonacci` | `(n : myN) → myN` | Fibonacci numbers with base cases `F(1) = 1`, `F(2) = 1`. |
| `div2` | `(n : myN) → myN` | Integer division by 2 in the 1-based natural setting (rounds down, with 1 as the floor — see *Possible Issues*). |
| `dist` | `(m n : myN) → myN` | Distance-like recursive difference function on naturals — see *Possible Issues* for its behavior on equal inputs. |

## Instances

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ToString myN` | `instance : ToString myN` | Uses `toStringMyN` for string rendering. |
| `Add myN` | `instance : Add myN` | Registers `myAdd` for the `+` operator. |
| `Mul myN` | `instance : Mul myN` | Registers `myMult` for the `*` operator. |

## Possible Issues

1. There is no zero in this 1-based `myN`. As the source itself notes (`chapter3.lean:90-96`),
   this means `binomial a b` returns `_1` whenever `a < b`, instead of the mathematically
   expected `0` — the same limitation affects `binomial_v2`.
2. For the same reason, `div2 n` for `n = 1` or `n = 2` both round down to `myN.one` (there is no
   `0` result to represent "less than one"), and `dist m n` returns `myN.one` (not a zero) when
   `m` and `n` denote the same number greater than 1 — e.g. `dist _2 _2` reduces to `myN.one`,
   not to any representation of "no distance". Callers relying on `dist m n = m` iff `m = n`
   should be aware of this.

# Namespace `chapter3_integers`

## Types and Constructors

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `myZ` | `Type` | Integer type encoded as `myN ⊕ (Unit ⊕ myN)` (negative / zero / positive). |
| `Zneg` | `(n : myN) → myZ` | Builds a negative integer. |
| `Zpos` | `(n : myN) → myZ` | Builds a positive integer. |
| `Zzero` | `myZ` | Zero integer constructor. |
| `__0` | `(U : Unit) → myZ` | Alternative zero term. **Note:** despite looking like a bare constant, `__0` actually takes an explicit `Unit` argument — it is defined after `variable (U : Unit)` (`chapter3.lean:174`) and its body references `U`, so Lean auto-prepends `(U : Unit)` to its signature. In practice it must be called as `__0 ()`. |

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `myNatToInt` | `(n : myN) → myZ` | Injects naturals into positive integers (alias for `Zpos`). |
| `negative` | `(n : myZ) → myZ` | Integer negation. |
| `showMyZ` | `(z : myZ) → String` | String view of integers (`"-n"`, `"0"`, `"n"`). |
| `predZ` | `(z : myZ) → myZ` | Integer predecessor operation. |
| `succZ` | `(z : myZ) → myZ` | Integer successor operation. |

## Instances

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Coe myN myZ` | `instance : Coe myN myZ` | Coercion from naturals to integers via `myNatToInt`. |

# Namespace `chapter3_booleans`

## Types

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `myBool.myTrue` | `myBool` | Boolean true constructor. |
| `myBool.myFalse` | `myBool` | Boolean false constructor. |
| `myProd.mk` | `{P Q : Type} → (x : P) → (y : Q) → myProd P Q` | Constructor for the custom product type. `P`, `Q` are implicit, as Lean makes inductive-family parameters implicit in every constructor. |
| `myEquiv` | `(P Q : Type) → Type` | Type equivalence as a pair of maps `P → Q` and `Q → P` (defined as `myProd (P → Q) (Q → P)`). |
| `myNegType` | `(P : Type) → Type` | Negation type (`P → Empty`). Picks up its `P` argument from the section `variable (P Q R : Type)` — see the note at the top of this document. |

## Function Summary

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `myNeg` | `(x : myBool) → myBool` | Boolean negation. |
| `myConj` | `(x y : myBool) → myBool` | Boolean conjunction (AND). |
| `myDisj` | `(x y : myBool) → myBool` | Boolean disjunction (OR). |
| `proj1` | `{P Q : Type} → (z : myProd P Q) → P` | First projection from `myProd`. |
| `proj2` | `{P Q : Type} → (z : myProd P Q) → Q` | Second projection from `myProd`. |
| `myProdFunc` | `{P Q R : Type} → (f : P → Q → R) → (myProd P Q → R)` | Converts a curried binary function into a function on a product input. |
| `double_neg` | `(P : Type) → P → myNegType (myNegType P)` | Introduction of double negation. Leading `(P : Type)` comes from the section variable (see note above). |
| `double_contrapositive` | `(P Q : Type) → (P → Q) → (myNegType (myNegType P) → myNegType (myNegType Q))` | Double-negation contrapositive transport across an implication. |
| `double_contrapositive_ii` | `(P Q : Type) → (P → myNegType (myNegType Q)) → (myNegType (myNegType P) → myNegType (myNegType Q))` | Variant of double-negation transport with a double-negated codomain. |
| `double_contrapositive_iii` | `(P : Type) → myNegType (myNegType (myNegType (myNegType P) → P))` | Higher-order negation principle over a classical-style implication. |

# Notes

- This chapter uses 1-based naturals (`myN.one` is the smallest natural) — there is no zero
  constructor, which is the root cause of the issues listed above. A separate, 0-based
  development lives in `chapter3_naturals_with_zero.lean`; see that file's documentation.
- Several constructions in the boolean namespace (`double_neg`, `double_contrapositive*`,
  `myNegType`) rely on Lean's section-`variable` auto-binding rather than declaring their type
  parameters locally — see the callout at the top of this document.
- `example` blocks in the source (`chapter3.lean:276-283`) are anonymous checks, not named
  declarations, so they are not listed as functions above.
